symbols.name: source length
symbols.meaning: The number of coordinates of a source vector.
symbols.quote: Here $s$ is the number of coordinates of a source vector, and $t$ is the number of coordinates of a target vector, with $s<t$ and $\gcd(s,t)=1$.

symbols.name: target length
symbols.meaning: The number of coordinates of a target vector.
symbols.quote: Here $s$ is the number of coordinates of a source vector, and $t$ is the number of coordinates of a target vector, with $s<t$ and $\gcd(s,t)=1$.

symbols.name: Gaussian width
symbols.meaning: The integer width parameter of the Gaussian weights.
symbols.quote: The integer $\alpha$ is the width parameter of the Gaussian weights.

symbols.name: source transform
symbols.meaning: The normalized Fourier transform of length s.
symbols.quote: $F_s$ and $F_t$ are the normalized Fourier transforms of length $s$ and $t$.

symbols.name: target transform
symbols.meaning: The normalized Fourier transform of length t.
symbols.quote: $F_s$ and $F_t$ are the normalized Fourier transforms of length $s$ and $t$.

symbols.name: source permutation
symbols.meaning: The coordinate permutation on vectors of length s, sending g to the vector with j-th entry g_{tj}.
symbols.quote: $P_s$ and $P_t$ are the coordinate permutations $(P_s g)_j=g_{tj}$ and $(P_t h)_m=h_{-sm}$ on vectors $g$ of length $s$ and $h$ of length $t$, with $j$ and $m$ the coordinate indices and subscripts taken modulo the length.

symbols.name: target permutation
symbols.meaning: The coordinate permutation on vectors of length t, sending h to the vector with m-th entry h_{-sm}.
symbols.quote: $P_s$ and $P_t$ are the coordinate permutations $(P_s g)_j=g_{tj}$ and $(P_t h)_m=h_{-sm}$ on vectors $g$ of length $s$ and $h$ of length $t$, with $j$ and $m$ the coordinate indices and subscripts taken modulo the length.

symbols.name: source vector
symbols.meaning: A vector of length s, the input of P_s.
symbols.quote: $P_s$ and $P_t$ are the coordinate permutations $(P_s g)_j=g_{tj}$ and $(P_t h)_m=h_{-sm}$ on vectors $g$ of length $s$ and $h$ of length $t$, with $j$ and $m$ the coordinate indices and subscripts taken modulo the length.

symbols.name: target vector
symbols.meaning: A vector of length t, the input of P_t.
symbols.quote: $P_s$ and $P_t$ are the coordinate permutations $(P_s g)_j=g_{tj}$ and $(P_t h)_m=h_{-sm}$ on vectors $g$ of length $s$ and $h$ of length $t$, with $j$ and $m$ the coordinate indices and subscripts taken modulo the length.

symbols.name: coordinate index
symbols.meaning: An index of a coordinate of a vector.
symbols.quote: $P_s$ and $P_t$ are the coordinate permutations $(P_s g)_j=g_{tj}$ and $(P_t h)_m=h_{-sm}$ on vectors $g$ of length $s$ and $h$ of length $t$, with $j$ and $m$ the coordinate indices and subscripts taken modulo the length.

symbols.name: target coordinate index
symbols.meaning: An index of a coordinate of a target-length vector.
symbols.quote: $P_s$ and $P_t$ are the coordinate permutations $(P_s g)_j=g_{tj}$ and $(P_t h)_m=h_{-sm}$ on vectors $g$ of length $s$ and $h$ of length $t$, with $j$ and $m$ the coordinate indices and subscripts taken modulo the length.

symbols.name: identity map
symbols.meaning: The identity map, which leaves every vector unchanged.
symbols.quote: $I$ is the identity map.

symbols.name: source Gaussian map
symbols.meaning: A Gaussian-weighted map from vectors of length s to vectors of length t.
symbols.quote: The identity rests on two Gaussian-weighted maps $S$ and $T$ from vectors of length $s$ to vectors of length $t$.

symbols.name: target Gaussian map
symbols.meaning: A Gaussian-weighted map from vectors of length s to vectors of length t.
symbols.quote: The identity rests on two Gaussian-weighted maps $S$ and $T$ from vectors of length $s$ to vectors of length $t$.

symbols.name: Gaussian diagonal map
symbols.meaning: The diagonal map on vectors of length s that multiplies coordinate j by a Gaussian factor.
symbols.quote: $D$ is the diagonal map on vectors of length $s$ that multiplies coordinate $j$ by a Gaussian factor, and $C$ selects from a length-$t$ vector the coordinates at the indices nearest $tj/s$, for $0\le j<s$.

symbols.name: selection map
symbols.meaning: The map from vectors of length t to vectors of length s that selects the coordinates at the indices nearest tj/s.
symbols.quote: $D$ is the diagonal map on vectors of length $s$ that multiplies coordinate $j$ by a Gaussian factor, and $C$ selects from a length-$t$ vector the coordinates at the indices nearest $tj/s$, for $0\le j<s$.

symbols.name: near-identity map
symbols.meaning: The map CTD from vectors of length s to themselves, which is close to the identity.
symbols.quote: Put $N=CTD$, a map close to $I$.

symbols.name: series index
symbols.meaning: The summation index of the Neumann series for N inverse.
symbols.quote: Its inverse is the Neumann series $N^{-1}=\sum_{r\ge 0}(I-N)^r$, where $r$ is the summation index.

symbols.name: scaled source map
symbols.meaning: The map S/2, a contraction from vectors of length s to vectors of length t.
symbols.quote: Fourth, set $A=S/2$ and $B_0=2^{-(2\alpha^2-2)}DN^{-1}C/2$.

symbols.name: scaled inverse map
symbols.meaning: The map 2^{-(2 alpha^2-2)} D N^{-1} C / 2, a contraction from vectors of length t to vectors of length s.
symbols.quote: Fourth, set $A=S/2$ and $B_0=2^{-(2\alpha^2-2)}DN^{-1}C/2$.

relations.quote: Gaussian resampling is a technique that replaces a [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md) of arbitrary length by transforms whose axis lengths are powers of two, which the integer multiplier needs.
